about.cadet: How to tell if an old picture was changed.
about.recruit: Three checks that show whether an old photo is real, or was changed later.
about.operative: Three checks for altered sources, and how much evidence a verdict needs.

cadet: OMNI hid old pictures from before it took over. The rebels call them Echoes.
But OMNI didn't only hide them. It changed some, so people would believe its story.
Before we keep a picture, we check it.
recruit: The rebels call a recovered photo or video from before OMNI an Echo.
OMNI didn't only erase the past. It changed some of it, so people would believe its version. A changed picture is altered.
So before an Echo leaves the Archive, we check its evidence: what the picture itself can prove.
operative: An Echo is a recovered photo or video from before OMNI: a primary source.
OMNI didn't only erase sources. It edited some and left them where people would find them, so the edits look like history. An edited source is altered.
A verdict needs evidence: something in the source, or about it, that proves it. A feeling isn't evidence.

cadet: • Too new? Is anything in it from later than the picture's date?
• Shadows: do all the shadows point the same way?
recruit: • A date that can't be right. Nothing in an Echo can be newer than its date. OMNI's hexagon in a 2034 photo is proof: OMNI was switched on in 2036.
• A shadow that doesn't match. In one photo, every shadow points away from the same light. A shadow pointing the other way was pasted in.
• Copies that disagree. When copies of the same Echo disagree, trust what most of them agree on.
operative: • A date that can't be right. Nothing in an Echo can be newer than its date (OMNI 2036, risk ratings 2042, Wardens 2046).
• A shadow that doesn't match. One light source means every shadow points the same way.
• Copies that disagree. Independent copies that agree outweigh the odd one out.
• The file record. Who saved it, and when. An edit by OMNI's archive after 2046 is a warning sign.
One proof is enough to call an Echo altered. Two independent proofs make it certain.

cadet: Guessing is not the same as knowing. Look at the clues first, then choose.
recruit: A real Echo passes every check. An altered one fails at least one. Make your first guess, then look for the proof before you decide. A right guess without proof is still a guess.
operative: Commit to a first call, then test it. If the evidence disagrees with your call, the evidence wins. A real source passes every check; an altered one fails at least one.

q.cadet: A picture says it's from long ago, but OMNI's sign is in it. OMNI wasn't made yet. Is it real?
q.recruit: A photo says 2034, but OMNI's hexagon is on a banner. OMNI was switched on in 2036. What does that prove?
q.operative: A photo dated 2034 shows OMNI's hexagon on a banner. OMNI was switched on in 2036. What does that prove?

recruit: It was saved in the wrong folder

explain.cadet: OMNI wasn't made yet, so someone added its sign later. The picture was changed.
explain.recruit: Nothing in an Echo can be newer than its date. The hexagon came in 2036, so someone added it later.
explain.operative: An object newer than the source's date can't be in it. The hexagon dates from 2036, so the photo was edited.

q.cadet: Two copies of a picture show lots of people. One copy shows empty seats. Which one was changed?
q.recruit: Three copies of the same photo: two show a full crowd, one shows empty seats. Which copy was altered?
q.operative: Three independent copies: two show a full crowd, one (saved by OMNI's archive in 2052) shows empty seats. Which was altered?

options: The ones with a full crowd

explain.cadet: Most copies show people, so the empty one was changed.
explain.recruit: When copies disagree, trust what most of them agree on. The odd one out is the altered copy.
explain.operative: Two independent copies agree; the odd one out, edited after the Day of Silence, is the altered one.
